baseline: Host prebuilt readv_test (gvisor release-20260622.0) passes 3/3 for this filter. Per assertion: (1) BadIovecBase_File (readv.cc:128) builds one iovec {iov_base=NULL, iov_len=0x400} and calls readv(test_file_fd_, iov, 1); the correct kernel returns -1/EFAULT. Note the mechanism: access_ok(NULL, 1024) *passes* on Linux (NULL is below TASK_SIZE), so EFAULT is produced later, when the copy to the unmapped zero page faults. This is delayed buffer validation, not an eager NULL rejection. (2) BadIovecBase_Pipe (readv.cc:136) is the same iovec against test_pipe_[0]; -1/EFAULT for the same reason. (3) IovecOutsideTaskAddressRangeInNonemptyArray (readv.cc:255) builds two iovecs, iov[0]={iov_base=(void*)-1, iov_len=0} and iov[1]={buf.data(), kReadvTestDataSize=284}, and calls readv(test_file_fd_, iov, 2); the correct kernel returns -1/EFAULT and copies nothing, even though the offending entry is zero-length. Here EFAULT is eager: access_ok(0xffffffffffffffff, 0) fails because the base alone exceeds TASK_SIZE, so the whole import aborts before any data moves. The two mechanisms are distinct and a correct fix must reproduce both. Cross-check with the sibling case that is NOT blocked and passes today, ReadvTest.NullIovecInNonemptyArray: iov[0]={NULL, 0}, iov[1]={buf, 284}, expected SyscallSucceedsWithValue(284) - so {base=0, len=0} must be skipped silently and must not error. Assertion strings and constants were read out of the prebuilt binary (objdump of each TestBody; kReadvTestDataSize = 0x11c = 284 at .rodata 0x1a10e0) because raw.githubusercontent.com, github.com, elixir.bootlin.com and codebrowser.dev are all blocked from this container.
failing_assertion: All 3 fail in Asterinas at e8f2b9ca6 (qemu.log lines 39-59, 0 passed). readv.cc:128 'Value of: readv(test_file_fd_.get(), iov, 1) Expected: -1 (failure), with errno PosixError(errno=14 Bad address) Actual: 0'. readv.cc:136 identical, Actual: 0 for the pipe. readv.cc:255 'Value of: readv(test_file_fd_.get(), iov, 2) ... Actual: 284' - i.e. Asterinas silently dropped the out-of-range iov[0] and copied all 284 bytes of iov[1].

impl.lines: 44-57 (IoVec::is_empty/reader/writer), 94-114 (copy_iovs_and_convert loop); the `base == 0` clause is line 47 and the skip is lines 108-110

root_cause: One defect in kernel/src/util/iovec.rs::copy_iovs_and_convert produces both wrong values, because the loop decides an entry is uninteresting before anything validates its base address. For each user iovec it builds an IoVec, then at lines 108-110 does `if iov.is_empty() { continue; }`, and IoVec::is_empty (line 46-48) is `self.len == 0 || self.base == 0`. Only entries surviving that filter reach convert_iovec, which is where IoVec::writer -> VmSpace::writer (ostd/src/mm/vm_space.rs:180-195) applies the sole address check in the path, `vaddr.saturating_add(len) > MAX_USERSPACE_VADDR => Error::AccessDenied` (mapped to EFAULT at kernel/src/error.rs:198). So the filter is also the validation bypass. Cases 1 and 2: the `|| self.base == 0` clause classifies {base=0, len=0x400} as empty, so the entry is dropped and no writer is created for it. do_sys_readv (kernel/src/syscall/preadv.rs:155-174) then iterates an empty writer array, never calls file.read, and returns Ok(0) at line 180 - so the read never touches address 0 and the page fault that should produce EFAULT never happens. The bug is not a missing NULL check; it is a NULL *special case* that suppresses the fault Linux relies on. That the same 0 is returned for both the regular file and the pipe confirms the defect is above the file object: neither InodeHandle nor the pipe is ever consulted. Case 3: the `self.len == 0` clause legitimately identifies {base=usize::MAX, len=0} as empty, but `continue` skips it *without ever range-checking base*, so the out-of-range address is never seen by VmSpace::writer. iov[1] is valid, is converted, and reads 284 bytes. The two clauses of one predicate thus cause the two different wrong answers. Note kernel/src/context.rs:95-124 documents that CurrentUserSpace::reader/writer deliberately omit check_vaddr_lowerbound to preserve delayed buffer validation - that design is correct and case 1 depends on it; iovec.rs breaks it by filtering the entry out before the deferred access can occur.
invariant: Every iovec entry supplied by userspace must have its base address validated against the user address range, and that validation must happen for all entries including zero-length ones, before any entry in the vector transfers data; an entry whose base is outside the user address range fails the whole call with EFAULT. Separately, a zero base is not itself invalid and must not be special-cased: an entry with a non-zero length and an unmapped base must be attempted so the access faults, which is what yields EFAULT, while an entry with zero length transfers nothing regardless of its base.
owning_layer: The iovec import layer in kernel/src/util/iovec.rs - copy_iovs_and_convert, which is the single shared entry point where user iovec arrays become VmReaderArray/VmWriterArray. This sits at syscall-entry level, above every FileLike and above the socket layer, and is the closest Asterinas equivalent to Linux's __import_iovec. Asterinas has no iov_iter abstraction, so this function is the only place that sees the whole vector before any transfer, which is what makes it the correct owner: the invariant is all-or-nothing across the vector, so it cannot be enforced by any per-entry consumer downstream. Fixing it in preadv.rs instead would leave pwritev and the socket paths defective. The lower ostd layer (VmSpace::writer) is the wrong owner too - it already implements the range check correctly and is simply never reached for filtered entries; the defect is that iovec.rs decides not to call it.
linux_reference: Linux enforces this in lib/iov_iter.c, in __import_iovec(), not in iovec_from_user(). iovec_from_user() only copies the array and validates lengths (nr_segs > UIO_MAXIOV => EINVAL; negative iov_len as ssize_t => EINVAL; array itself unreadable => EFAULT via user_access_begin/unsafe_get_user). __import_iovec() then runs the per-entry base check over the whole vector before any I/O: `for (seg = 0; seg < nr_segs; seg++) { ssize_t len = (ssize_t)iov[seg].iov_len; if (!access_ok(iov[seg].iov_base, len)) { if (iov != *iovp) kfree(iov); *iovp = NULL; return -EFAULT; } ... }`. Two properties matter here. First, the check is not gated on len, so a zero-length entry with an out-of-range base still fails the entire import - that is exactly case 3, since x86 __access_ok is `size <= TASK_SIZE && addr <= TASK_SIZE - size`, which rejects addr=0xffffffffffffffff even at size 0. Second, access_ok is a range test only and never rejects NULL, so cases 1 and 2 get past import and fault at copy time - which is why Linux returns EFAULT rather than 0 for a 1024-byte read into NULL, and why Asterinas's delayed-validation design is compatible with the expected result. So the placement is: generic iovec import, above the VFS and above the socket layer, applied once per vector. (nr_segs == 1 short-circuits to __import_iovec_ubuf -> import_ubuf, which applies its own access_ok(buf, len) - same semantics, different path. mm/process_vm_access.c calls iovec_from_user directly and deliberately skips access_ok because the addresses belong to another process; this replaced the old CHECK_IOVEC_ONLY sentinel in rw_copy_check_uvector. Structure dates from Christoph Hellwig's Sept 2020 series 'iov_iter: refactor rw_copy_check_uvector and import_iovec'; David Laight's March 2025 'iov: Remove access_ok() from import_iovec()' proposed deleting these checks and was not merged, so treat them as live behavior.)
other_callers: Not narrow - six call sites share the defective function, so the layer choice is load-bearing. kernel/src/syscall/preadv.rs:90 (do_sys_preadv, serving preadv and preadv2) and :155 (do_sys_readv, serving readv and preadv2 with offset -1); kernel/src/syscall/pwritev.rs:91 (do_sys_pwritev) and :151 (do_sys_writev); kernel/src/util/net/socket.rs:167 (copy_reader_array_from_user, sendmsg/sendmmsg) and :178 (copy_writer_array_from_user, recvmsg/recvmmsg). Every one of these accepts a user iovec array and every one currently drops a {base=0, len>0} entry and skips range validation on a zero-length entry. The write direction is the more serious half: writev with {base=NULL, len=n} silently reports 0 bytes written instead of EFAULT, and a caller that retries on a short write cannot distinguish that from a full buffer. There is no gvisor blocklist entry for writev_test and no writev_test binary in /root/syscall_test_bins (only readv_test and readv_socket_test), so nothing in the suite currently guards the write side - which is precisely why the fix belongs in iovec.rs rather than in preadv.rs. In-tree regression guards that must keep passing: ReadvTest.NullIovecInNonemptyArray ({base=0,len=0} must still be skipped and return 284, not EFAULT) and ReadvTest.ZeroIovecs_File / ZeroIovecs_Pipe, all currently unblocked and green.
suggested_direction: Fix in copy_iovs_and_convert (kernel/src/util/iovec.rs:94-114) so that validation precedes filtering, and split the two conflated conditions. Concretely: (a) drop the `|| self.base == 0` clause from IoVec::is_empty (line 47) so a zero base is no longer treated as an absent buffer - an entry with len > 0 then gets a writer/reader and the access faults naturally, which is how cases 1 and 2 turn into EFAULT and is consistent with the delayed-validation contract documented at kernel/src/context.rs:99-113; (b) range-check every entry's base before the `continue` at lines 108-110, so a zero-length entry with an out-of-range base still fails the whole call. For (b), the check must match what VmSpace::writer already applies - `base.saturating_add(len) > MAX_USERSPACE_VADDR => EFAULT` - so the natural shape is to hoist that comparison into the loop ahead of the emptiness test rather than to invent a second rule; reusing the same predicate keeps the eager path and the lazy path from disagreeing about what is in range. Keep the existing documented invariant that the returned array contains no empty readers/writers (relied on by the debug_assert! at preadv.rs:157 and pwritev.rs:106, and by the empty-array probe at preadv.rs:94-99), so zero-length entries must still be excluded from the array after being validated. Do the validation for all `count` entries before returning any converted entry, so the call is all-or-nothing as in Linux and no data moves when a later entry is bad - iov[1] must not be read in case 3. The truncation to MAX_TOTAL_IOV_BYTES at lines 103-106 is unrelated and should be left alone. Since the change is in shared code, the two remaining blocked readv cases (ReadvTestNoFixture.TruncatedAtMax, TruncatedAtMax_NoRandomSave) stay blocked and out of scope, and ReadvTest.NotReadable_Pipe - already stale-green per select.json - should not be unblocked in this commit.
